Empirical Research Plan: “How Do Debt Covenants Influence Corporate Investment?”

============================================================
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------
Main design: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) at the covenant threshold.

Why FRD?  
• The covenant establishes an explicit, numeric cutoff (e.g., leverage ≤ 3.0, interest-coverage ≥ 2.0). Crossing that cutoff sharply raises the probability that the covenant becomes binding (default declaration, waiver negotiations, higher spreads, extra monitoring).  
• Firms that are infinitesimally above and below the threshold are ex-ante comparable; the distance to the covenant (the “cushion”) provides a quasi-random assignment to greater financing constraints.  
• It is “fuzzy” because some violations may be waived, and some lenders may act pre-emptively if the cushion becomes very small; i.e. the probability—but not certainty—of treatment jumps at the cutoff.

A complementary event-time DiD/event-study around the first covenant violation can serve as robustness, but the FRD will be the headline estimator.

============================================================
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------
Running variable (RV):  
cushion_it = ( actual ratio_it – covenant threshold_i ) / |threshold_i|.  
We multiply by –1 when the covenant is a maximum (e.g., leverage) so that smaller values always mean “worse.”  
RV = 0 at the threshold; RV < 0 implies a breach.

Treatment indicator D_it:  
D_it = 1 if the covenant is binding (actual breach OR formal waiver negotiation initiated) in firm-year t, 0 otherwise.

Treatment group (just below cutoff):  
Firm-years with –h ≤ RV_it < 0.

Control group (just above cutoff):  
Firm-years with 0 ≤ RV_it ≤ h.

Bandwidth h will be data-driven (Calonico–Cattaneo–Titiunik optimal bandwidth) and varied in robustness checks.

Event date/timing:  
Because covenants are continuously monitored, the relevant “treatment” occurs within the fiscal year in which RV crosses zero. We treat firm-years, not firms, as treated units.

============================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential investment outcomes in RV at 0.  
 Plausibility: firms do not make large discrete changes in investment exactly at an arbitrary numeric covenant level absent the covenant’s legal trigger.

A2. No precise manipulation of RV around 0.  
 Potential concern: managers could engage in accounting management to stay just above the threshold. Plausible but testable—address with McCrary density test and discontinuity tests in observable covariates.

A3. First-stage relevance—probability of binding constraint jumps at 0.  
 Plausible: lenders obtain legal rights only after breach. We will show a strong first-stage jump in waiver negotiations, spread increases, or reductions in credit line availability.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA).  
 Investment decisions of one firm do not directly affect another’s treatment probability within the narrow band—reasonable in this context.

A5. Local representativeness.  
 The causal effect is LATE for firms near the threshold; generalization beyond the local margin requires caution.

============================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Accounting manipulation / sorting near cutoff.  
• McCrary density test on RV.  
• Discontinuity tests on lagged variables.  
• Use “hard” ratios less prone to manipulation (e.g., EBITDA-interest) and focus on unexpected earnings components (after Jones-type adjustment).

T2. Multiple simultaneous covenants (multiple thresholds).  
• Focus on the covenant that is closest to breach each year (“tightest covenant”).  
• Include controls for the distance to other covenants.  
• Show robustness restricting to loans with a single binding covenant.

T3. Measurement error in identifying the threshold.  
• Collect actual covenant levels from SEC filings/LPC Dealscan.  
• Drop observations where covenant level is imputed or ambiguous.  
• Instrument actual breach with an indicator for “predicted breach” using prior-year cushion to create an even cleaner first stage (secondary IV robustness).

============================================================
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#----------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)        # fast fixed-effects regressions
library(rdrobust)      # RD estimation
library(ggplot2)
#----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load Data
#----------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("compustat_covenants_1996_2005.csv")   # one row per firm-year

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable Construction
#----------------------------------------------------------
# Example: leverage covenant (max) and interest-coverage covenant (min)
# Choose the covenant with smallest absolute cushion each year
dt[, cushion_lev := (max_leverage_threshold - actual_leverage) / abs(max_leverage_threshold)]
dt[, cushion_cov := (actual_icr - min_icr_threshold) / abs(min_icr_threshold)]

# Harmonise sign: negative = breach
dt[, cushion_lev := -cushion_lev]   # leverage covenant flipped
# tightest covenant
dt[, abs_cushion_lev := abs(cushion_lev)]
dt[, abs_cushion_cov := abs(cushion_cov)]
dt[, tightest := fifelse(abs_cushion_lev < abs_cushion_cov, "lev", "cov")]
dt[, RV := ifelse(tightest=="lev", cushion_lev, cushion_cov)]

# Treatment: formal breach or waiver
dt[, D := breach_flag]                        # 1 if formal breach that year
dt[, invest := capx / lag(total_assets)]      # investment ratio
dt[, controls := .(cash_flow = oibdp/lag(total_assets),
                   size = log(lag(total_assets)),
                   q = tobins_q)]

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main FRD Estimation
#----------------------------------------------------------
# First stage: effect on probability of breach (check jump)
rd_first <- rdrobust(y = dt$D, x = dt$RV, c = 0)
print(rd_first$coef)

# Reduced form: effect on investment
rd_rf <- rdrobust(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, c = 0)
print(rd_rf$coef)

# Wald estimator (fuzzy RD local Wald)
tau_hat <- rd_rf$coef["tau.us"] / rd_first$coef["tau.us"]
print(tau_hat)

# Convenient wrapper in rdrobust can do fuzzy automatically:
rd_fuzzy <- rdrobust(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, fuzzy = dt$D, c = 0)
summary(rd_fuzzy)

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness: Different Bandwidth & Polynomials
#----------------------------------------------------------
rd_fuzzy_narrow <- rdrobust(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, fuzzy = dt$D,
                            bwselect = "mserd", p = 1, c = 0)
rd_fuzzy_wide   <- rdrobust(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, fuzzy = dt$D,
                            h = 0.10, p = 2, c = 0)   # ±10% cushion

# Plot
rdplot(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, c = 0, p = 1, h = rd_fuzzy$h_l)

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Placebo Cutoff at ±0.10
#----------------------------------------------------------
rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = dt$invest, x = dt$RV, fuzzy = dt$D, c = 0.10)
summary(rd_placebo)
```

============================================================
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------
Prediction: Binding covenants (treatment) reduce investment.  
Magnitude: Prior literature (e.g., Chava & Roberts 2008) suggests a drop of roughly 30 bp in investment/assets. For firms near the cutoff, I expect a local average treatment effect of –0.02 to –0.03 (i.e., a 2–3 percentage-point lower capex-to-assets ratio) relative to a mean of ~0.12.

============================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No sorting/manipulation near cutoff ………………… 0.8  
C2. Continuity in other covariates at cutoff ………… 0.8  
C3. Correct functional-form / bandwidth choice ……… 0.7  
C4. Strong first stage (jump in breach prob.) ……… 1.0  
C5. No other shocks exactly at cutoff …………………… 0.8  

Average ≈ 0.82 → overall confidence: “good but verify.”

============================================================
This plan provides a transparent, testable causal estimate of how financing constraints triggered by covenant breaches affect firm investment, with code and diagnostics to back up the design.
